finding.title: Rewrite docs/data-models.md — it self-contradicts on schemaVersion and describes the extinct pre-rebuild schema

evidence.quote: User DB — schema v4, 23 tables, 20 DAOs. Read-write.
The schema stands at v15 with incremental migrations from v1.

finding.why: The doc disagrees with itself (v4 at the top, v15 in its own Migration History table) and both numbers are wrong against the real schemaVersion 32. Its ER diagram and table sections (lines 65-712) have no Outbox, CompletionEvents, StreakEvents, DailyPlans, or TrackLearningOrder tables — the actual backbone of the append-only ledger and sync-outbox architecture that architecture.md and delete-policy.md describe as central. It also names the Firestore path `profiles/{profileId}` where the real path (confirmed in api-contracts.md and firestore.rules) is `learner_profiles/{profileId}`. A contributor or agent using this file to understand 'what tables exist' before a schema change gets an actively wrong model of the persistence layer.
finding.recommendation: Regenerate data-models.md's table/ER/Firestore sections from the current Drift table classes (reuse tool/gen_arch_tables.dart's output, already authoritative for architecture.md), set schemaVersion to 32/5/1 consistently, and correct the learner_profiles path.
acceptance_criteria: docs/data-models.md states schemaVersion 32 (User DB) / 5 (Content DB) / 1 (Registry DB) in exactly one internally-consistent place
docs/data-models.md's table list includes Outbox, CompletionEvents, StreakEvents, DailyPlans, TrackLearningOrder
docs/data-models.md's Firestore collection path reads learner_profiles, matching docs/api-contracts.md and firestore.rules

finding.title: Document the tutor-mode Firestore/Functions surface in docs/api-contracts.md and fix the stale 'indexes.json is empty' claim

evidence.quote: **Live layout — `users/{uid}/...`** — every path is owner-gated by `isOwner(uid)`:
Firestore indexes | firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes | firestore.indexes.json (currently empty)

finding.why: functions/src/index.ts exports 26 Cloud Functions today, not 4 — 22 of them (inviteTutor, acceptTutorInvite, revokeTutorGrant, tutorResetCompletion, tutorUpsertTrack, etc.) implement the entire tutor cross-user-access feature and are undocumented. firestore.rules has ~150 lines of top-level `tutor_grants`/`tutor_active_access` rules granting non-owner (tutor) reads on a child's records — directly at odds with api-contracts.md's characterization that 'every path is owner-gated'. firestore.indexes.json is not empty; it has 6 composite indexes, all for tutor_grants queries. This is the most privacy-sensitive feature in the codebase (cross-user access to a child's learning data, gated by SR-5) and the canonical API-contracts reference does not mention it exists.
finding.recommendation: Add a Tutor Mode section to api-contracts.md covering tutor_grants/tutor_active_access collections, the tutor read carve-outs in firestore.rules, the 22 tutor* Cloud Functions, and the 6 composite indexes; fix the 'indexes.json is empty' line in both api-contracts.md and deployment-guide.md.
acceptance_criteria: api-contracts.md's Cloud Functions table lists all 26 exported functions from functions/src/index.ts (or explicitly groups the tutor_* ones with a count)
api-contracts.md documents tutor_grants and tutor_active_access as top-level collections
api-contracts.md and deployment-guide.md no longer claim firestore.indexes.json is empty
